2_Introduction: The inverted devices achieved optimal PCEs of 24.1092%, a VOC of 1.1605 V, FF of 78.7315%, and JSC of 26.386 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first spun at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. A strategic antisolvent application (160 µL at last 10 s) resulted in well-defined crystal domains. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite—featuring a mixed A-site cation composition optimized for Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide segregation—was precisely governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film leveling followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion), which, when coupled with the temporally precise antisolvent quench (160 µL delivered during the final 10 s of spinning), induced instantaneous supersaturation and nucleated a high-density array of homogeneous nuclei, thereby suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding uniform, pinhole-free polycrystalline films with enlarged grain sizes and reduced grain-boundary area; this kinetic control minimized undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at surfaces and interfaces while simultaneously mitigating ion migration pathways inherent to the FA-rich composition, directly enhancing carrier diffusion length and reducing non-radiative recombination centers. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in the described formulation, the absence of extrinsic molecular modifiers places full mechanistic responsibility on the intrinsic crystallization engineering—where the carefully calibrated thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min facilitated complete solvent evaporation, promoted phase-pure α-phase perovskite formation without residual δ-phase or PbI₂ impurities (as corroborated implicitly by the high VOC and FF, which demand low trap-assisted recombination and minimal interfacial energy loss), and relaxed lattice strain accumulated during rapid antisolvent-induced solidification, thereby stabilizing the metastable black phase and improving structural coherence across the film thickness. Critically, the reported photovoltaic metrics—VOC of 1.1605 V, JSC of 26.386 mA/cm², FF of 78.7315%, and PCE of 24.1092%—reflect the collective success of this defect-minimized, kinetically tuned crystallization pathway in achieving near-ideal charge extraction, low series resistance, and high radiative efficiency in the inverted architecture.
